title: Common
description:
Primitives shared across every Halyard contract. $id values are stable identifiers, not URLs to fetch. Derived from SPEC sections 6, 8, 10 and 18.

The definitions live in $defs and are aliased under components/schemas. This is not redundancy: JSON Schema generators address them as #/$defs/X, while oapi-codegen only accepts depth-4 pointers and rejects #/$defs/X outright. The aliases are one-line $refs, so there is still exactly one definition of each type and the OpenAPI files reuse the very same generated Go types via -import-mapping.

Timestamp.title: Timestamp
Timestamp.description: RFC 3339, always UTC. Ads reporting is timezone-bound per account (SPEC 19.4) and converts at the edge of the system, never in storage.

Slug.title: Slug
Slug.description: Lowercase, DNS-label safe: a project slug reaches a preview hostname (SPEC 9).

GitSha.title: GitSha
GitSha.description: Full or abbreviated. SPEC 18 demotes these in the UI but never hides them.

Credits.title: Credits
Credits.description: A decimal string, not a number. The control plane stores credits as numeric(14,4) (SPEC 6) and SPEC 16.1 requires a ledger rather than a counter; routing money through an IEEE-754 double loses that exactness silently. Negative values are legal: SPEC 16.1 allows a bounded negative float rather than killing a running turn.

Role.title: Role
Role.description: SPEC 8. Approving anything that spends money requires owner or admin.

Error.title: Error
Error.description: SPEC 10 requires a structured error the UI can render as a human-readable message rather than a raw git error, and SPEC 18 requires errors to say what happened and how to fix it, without apologising. `fix` is that second half, and is separate from `message` so the UI can present it as an action.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable. Clients branch on this, never on `message`.

message.description: What happened, in the interface's voice.

fix.description: What the reader can do about it. Omitted only when nothing can be.

retriable.description: Whether repeating the identical request could succeed.

details.description: Code-specific context. Never contains a secret value (SPEC 17.2).

request_id.description: For correlating with traces and support requests.

Page.title: Page
Page.description: Cursor pagination. Offsets skip or duplicate rows when the underlying list changes, which it constantly does for timelines and ledgers.

next_cursor.description: Opaque. Null when this is the last page.
